rationale: Across the testimonials, a common theme is the significant role of community health workers in educating their communities about various health issues, encouraging preventive measures, and facilitating access to necessary medical care. This proactive approach to health education and intervention is seen in the way these workers identify health risks, provide advice, and refer individuals to medical facilities for treatment.

They also emphasize the importance of continuous learning and awareness, as well as the role of health education in promoting preventive measures and timely medical care.

concept: Empowerment through Health Education and Referral
rationale: The testimonials consistently highlight the role of community health workers in educating community members about various health issues, guiding them towards appropriate health services, and providing emotional support. This process empowers community members to better understand their health conditions and take appropriate actions.
examples: Speaker 1: Having come across three cases of pneumonia from an elderly, adolescent and middle aged woman, I referred them to Kuoyo dispensary and was given medication currently they are doing well.

Speaker 2: As I was teaching about HIV/AIDS, I had a client who had decided not to continue taking his ARV's because of the side effects he was experiencing. I took him through counselling not only on HIV/AIDS but also nutrition.

Speaker 9: I shared with them about the CHW training I underwent which was organized by wired international, the training that was an eye opener towards changing my habit of drinking. Through the training, I learnt about the effects of drinking too much alcohol and the benefits of quitting alcohol.

concept: Empowerment through Health Education
rationale: Across the testimonials, a common theme is the transformative power of health education. Community health workers are not only providing information but also empowering individuals and communities to take control of their health. This is seen in the changes in behavior, attitudes, and practices following health education sessions on various topics such as water treatment, menstrual hygiene, nutrition, immunization, and mental health.
examples: Speaker 1: We informed our participants to ensure that they consume clean and safe water on daily basis.
Speaker 2: They realized that they are also indirect menstruators and promised to help their wives emotionally or physically during their periods.
Speaker 3: After the health education I called them aside talked to them and counselled them on the importance of nutrition.
Speaker 4: After receiving the message on the importance of immunizations she agreed to take her child to the health center.
Speaker 8: I cancelled her and teach her on how she can manage herself with the children because the more she thanks she will be depressed.

concept: The Role of Community Health Workers in Malaria Prevention and Treatment
rationale: The testimonials highlight the crucial role of community health workers (CHWs) in educating communities about malaria prevention, recognizing symptoms, and ensuring proper treatment. They also emphasize the importance of CHWs in correcting misconceptions and harmful practices, such as self-medication.
examples: Imelda Anyango: As a CHW, what I can do to help people with malaria is to advise them to go to the hospital and get tested and also to be treated well whenever the symptoms occur.
Julliet Omollo: As a Community Health Worker, if you once identify someone suffering from malaria, I immediately refer to the nearest health center.
Daniel Ayieko: Now that I am a trained Community Health Worker, I have been training my community members on how they can prevent contacting malaria.
